newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends barely higher, stock hike due.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends barely higher, stock hike due.

text.p: COMEX copper ended barely higher after the day's healthy gains were largely pared by the close despite only a modest hike in LME stocks anticipated by traders for Friday after the recent sharp increases.
"We again failed to hold at these higher levels -- it appears to be having problems holding 110.00 cents in March," Smith Barney's David Rinehimer said.
"The market is just chopping around looking for direction. We are looking to see if in fact the supply situation is easing enough to allow prices to work lower," Rinehimer added.
LME stocks are expected to rise 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes Friday as the London backwardation eases, proving less of a magnet for metal, traders said.
March COMEX settled 0.10 cent firmer at 108.05 cents per pound, traded 110.20 to 107.90 cents.
The LME cash to three months premium or backwardation eased slightly Thursday, down by a few dollars to $96/$100 from Wednesday.

Traders did not expect LME depots in the U.S. to show any major increase in stocks Friday as the strong LME cash premium over spot COMEX, which drew the metal into the warehouses, has switched to a New York premium, but still too weak to provoke a flow of material in the opposite direction.
